rows.grounds: compound paragotra+kṛta, performed for a different gotra
intensified compound indicating extremely small amount
result or reward of an act

items.question: What degree of fruit results from performing rites for another lineage?
premises: A rite may be performed for another lineage.
Ritual acts produce fruit for their performer or beneficiary.
The verse specifies the quantity of fruit in this case.
items.inference: Therefore, performing such a rite for another lineage yields only very little fruit.
uncertainties: Whether paragotrakṛte qualifies a specific rite from the preceding verses or rites in general is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: And indeed, when done for another lineage, one would obtain only very little fruit.
